newsitem.title: JAPAN: JSDA backs appropriate decontrol of broking fees.
newsitem.headline: JSDA backs appropriate decontrol of broking fees.

text.p: The liberalisation of commissions on stock broking must be implemented along with deregulation of other business by securities houses, Masashi Suzuki, chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers Association, told reporters on Wednesday.

In Suzuki's first statement since Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto announced a five-year "Big Bang" financial reform plan last week, he said it was not appropriate to resist the planned changes to the stock broking commission system.
But he said the liberalisation must be implemented along with the deregulation of other business conducted by securities houses, and a review of the current stock transaction system.

In the Big Bang plan aimed at making Japan's financial market, free, fair and global over the next five years, Hashimoto asked Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka to take measures which included the liberalisation of financial market commission fees.

Suzuki also said that to improve services to customers investing in securities products, including money market funds, the securities industry will seek to join an ATM (automatic telling machines) network offered by banks.
He said the industry will ask the banking sector for access to the network shortly.
